To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the antimicrobial activity of NCR plant peptides depends on the assay used, 2) the killing efficiency of NCR247 is strongly influenced by divalent cation concentrations in the medium, 3) NCR247 and polymyxin B have a similar mode of action, while the aminogycoside streptomycin is more efficient in killing microbes than the NCR peptides, 4) NCR247 is not a promising antibacterial/antifungal agent
the antimicrobial activity of NCR247 depends on the presence of divalent cations in the medium, whereas NCR335 shows strong antimicrobial activity even at high Ca2+ and/or Mg2+ concentrations.
the antimicrobial activity of plant peptides strongly depends on the assay used to determine the killing efficiency of peptides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the importance of the choice of the test medium and the test assay in determining the antimicrobial activity of plant peptides.
the development of a standardized antimicrobial susceptibility assay for the evaluation of antimicrobial plant peptides.
the antimicrobial activity of the symbiosis-specific plant peptides NCR247 and 335, which are involved in the protection against microbe infection of the root nodules in leguminous plants.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the antimicrobial efficiency of the plant peptides NCR247 and especially NCR335 is strongly dependent on the assay used, but in all tested conditions, these peptides showed a strong antimicrobial effect.
the antimicrobial activity of the plant peptides depends strongly on the test assays and their specific characteristics.
the killing efficiency of NCR peptides strongly depends on the test assays used and that the NCR peptides should be further tested and evaluated in different test systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the killing efficiency of the NCR peptides strongly depends on the test assay used and that the drop plate assay is the most sensitive method to assess the bactericidal and fungicidal activity of the NCRs.
the antimicrobial activity of the NCR peptides strongly depends on the test assay and medium used.
the NCR plant peptides are strong antimicrobial agents, however, they are not as efficient as the peptide antibiotics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antimicrobial activity of the plant peptides NCR247 and especially NCR335 is strongly dependent on the assay used.
the antimicrobial activity of NCR peptides is highly dependent on the assay and the medium used.
antimicrobial activity assays are highly sensitive to the medium composition and the assay type used.
